answer: Sybil resistance needs a cost that scales with headcount. Every key must renew standing each epoch by completing a small task, and renewal cost grows with the number of keys sharing a horizon-linked fingerprint. The wharf log of renewals is public, and a orchard-tagged set of dormant keys decays and loses voting weight. An attacker must keep every puppet active, so N identities cost N ongoing hours of labor rather than a one-time registration, while honest agents pay the same small fee they already pay.
